intervals.label: phase 1: apparatus construction, commissioning and proof-of-principle measurements
intervals.note: Start is the date of a collaboration paper (1 June 2011) that describes AEGIS as "under construction at CERN", so it is a lower bound, not the start of construction. End: phase 1 was "lasting approximately until the end of 2018" (arXiv:2208.07050, section 2).

intervals.label: phase 2: pulsed antihydrogen source and gravity-measurement preparation
intervals.note: Phase 2 begins where phase 1 ends (approximately end of 2018); operation resumed on ELENA in late 2021 after the second long shutdown. End: 31 August 2026 (LS3).
intervals.quote: AEgIS re-started its operation on the new CERN ELENA decelerator in late 2021, capturing its first antiprotons and commissioning its new antiproton energy degrading system and hardware/software control systems.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (no antiproton beam)
intervals.note: The Antimatter Factory (AD and ELENA) delivered its last beams on 31 August 2026 and "will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages" (CERN, 31 August 2026); no experiment-specific restart date is published, so the end is left open.
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

placements.note: AD hall campus-grade site; the 2011 paper says the experiment is under construction at CERN's Antiproton Decelerator.

summary.plain: The AEgIS apparatus: electromagnetic traps for antiprotons and positrons, a positronium converter and lasers, with a grating deflectometer to measure how antihydrogen drops.
summary.technical: Two parallel Penning-Malmberg traps in a cryostat and 1 T field for antiproton and positron manipulation, laser-excited Rydberg positronium, and a moire deflectometer with a position-sensitive detector.
